entries.stanceLine: Backdrop favours upside breaks — The obvious draw (PDH 10589.4) sits beyond what's left of a typical day's range — targets past it are stretch-only today.

signals.text: The obvious draw (PDH 10589.4) sits beyond what's left of a typical day's range — targets past it are stretch-only today.
Sterling is at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range and still rising — a persistent FX headwind capping upside breaks (weak GBP is what lifts FTSE).
UK Labour Market Report @ 07:00 BST today — pre-release breaks are positioning, not conviction.
FTSE is tracking a firmer European tape (Euro Stoxx +0.94%) — the cross-market lean is up.
GBP is a crowded short — a short-squeeze higher in sterling is a latent slap for upside breaks (strong GBP weighs on FTSE).

entries.aiStanceLine: Due to 64% of the 14-day ADR already consumed, sterling pinned at its 89th 20-day percentile, and neither the ORB high nor low yet broken, upside breaks today look range-starved and currency-capped — favour long entries only on clean reclaims of 10,520 with modest targets, not trend-day sizing.
aiBullets: Only ~48 points of the 134.4-point ADR remain after today's 64% usage — the Prior Day High at 10,589.4 is arithmetically a stretch target, not a realistic first objective for an ORB long.

Copper's +2.54% surge and Euro Stoxx +0.94% both support the bull lean, yet neither has catalysed an ORB high break above 10,520.2 in the nine minutes since open — price hesitation despite sector tailwinds is a caution flag.

The gap-up of 60.5pts (0.58%) means the index opened into a partially exhausted range; combined with a crowded-short GBP at the 89th percentile, a reversal squeeze in sterling could rapidly turn a long break into a fakeout.
Tomorrow's UK CPI (07:00 BST, HIGH impact) sits just 23 hours away — any ORB long held overnight carries live inflation-repricing risk that could gap the position adversely.
